questionText:
Consider the following statements about the functionality of an IP based router.

I. A router does not modify the IP packets during forwarding.
II. It is not necessary for a router to implement any routing protocol.
III. A router should reassemble IP fragments if the MTU of the outgoing link is larger than the size of the incoming IP packet.

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
explanation:
Statement I is FALSE: During packet forwarding, a router modifies the IP header of the packet by decrementing the TTL (Time To Live) field and recalculating the header checksum.

Statement II is TRUE: It is not mandatory for a router to run dynamic routing protocols (e.g., RIP, OSPF, BGP) if static routing or default routing is configured manually.

Statement III is FALSE: Fragment reassembly is performed exclusively at the final destination host, not by intermediate routers, to minimize processing overhead on routers.
